newsitem.title: LATVIA: SWEDBANK SEES GDP GROWTH, SELL-OFFS AS CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SWEDBANK SEES GDP GROWTH, SELL-OFFS AS CHALLENGE.

text.p: Swedbank said on Tuesday that Latvia's economy seems to have recovered from the banking crisis and there were good growth prospects ahead while privatisation and legal reform remained a challenge.
The Swedish bank in a report on Latvia forecast gross domestic product (GDP) of three percent in the coming years.
"Inflation is expected to range between 10 to 15 percent during the next two years," Swedbank added, but noted the liberalisation of energy prices could lead to more inflation.
It also noted that the eight-party coalition government, led by Prime Minister Andris Shkele, was showing determination to complete privatisation in two years time.
Big infrastructure companies, including shipping, electricity and oil firms are on the list for 1997, it added.
Swedbank said that continued legal reforms were among the most important challenges Latvia faced in the coming years.
A vast bureaucracy and an unclear legal framework were mentioned by foreign companies among the reasons for a slower pace of sell-offs, Swedbank added.
"The current account deficit of three percent is expected to remain stable for the coming years," Swedbank said.
"In comparison to the neighbouring countries this deficit is more easily manageable," it added.
It also said that state finances were in good order and that foreign debt was low at around 10 percent of GDP.
